title: Ordering the VPS from the installer
body:
`installer` installs onto a server the client already has (address plus key or password). Ordering the VPS from a
provider is not built; the OVH Public Cloud API is multi-step (project, flavor, image, SSH key, polling) and cannot be
tested without a real account. Deferred (2026-10-04): clients order the server themselves.

Moved from catenahq/ops#297.

title: An installer leg has no bound of its own
body:
With 60% packet loss on the host, an install leg's output drained so slowly that nothing ended it for 77 minutes; the
test bench now fails such a run at 15 minutes, the product still waits. Each leg's output is kept on the server in
`/var/lib/catena/install/logs`, which a reconnect can read. Where the loss stops the install is chance: some runs aborted
in the release fetch (a layer timed out on all three reads), another got every layer through on retries and reached the
swarm deploys, each attempt bounded at 600 s (`swarm_stack_deploy_timeout`) and retried on rc=124, so the install ran
past 900 s.

- **Behaviour:** the installer bounds each leg as a whole: its retries run inside one overall bound, and a leg that
  reaches it ends with a plain message naming what did not answer (the registry, for a pull). An idle bound on the
  stream, or the starter recording its result on the host so a lost stream is re-read on reconnect.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** an install under 60% packet loss ends within 900 s with that message (the test bench's registry pull
  timeout scenario).

Moved from catenahq/ops#313.

title: The Actions tab's restart and wiring buttons run without the host lock
body:
The cloudflared restart button (`cloudflared-restart` in `ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/templates/actions.yml.j2`) takes no lock; Sync all does (c699adb). The Portainer restart button and the app wiring buttons are gone from the catalog (14b855b, 1869b3d, fa2831c, 6fb8a65).

- **Behaviour:** the cloudflared restart answers busy, in English and French, while another job holds `/run/catena.lock`.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test for the button, as `test_sync_all_starts_a_fresh_run.py`.

Moved from catenahq/ops#327.

title: Sync all may show the unit's last lines instead of its fresh run
body:
The Sync all button (`ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/templates/actions.yml.j2` `sync_fresh`) reads

title: Swarm task containers are picked by name pattern and head -n1, so an orphan can be chosen
body:
`ansible/reconcile/roles/`. Sites that resolve a swarm service's container with
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E '<swarm_container_regex(...)>' | head -n1`:
`oauth2_proxy/tasks/validate.yml:184-186,239,268`, `keycloak/tasks/_master_login.yml:22`,
`keycloak/tasks/provision_db.yml:29,73`, `keycloak/tasks/realm_bootstrap.yml:144,161,232,625`,
`keycloak/tasks/realm_export.yml:41`, `keycloak/tasks/validate.yml:30,131,183,197`, `postgres/tasks/main.yml:95`,
`postgres/tasks/validate.yml:24`, and `playbooks/validate.yml:119`.

`swarm_container_regex` is `^stack_service\\.slot\\.[a-z0-9]+$`, which pins no task id. Two containers of one service differ
only in that suffix, so `head -n1` takes whichever `docker ps` lists first. A container swarm has already replaced (an
orphan running the configuration it died with) is chosen as often as the live one: a validate probe then reports a
service healthy from the wrong container, and a task that execs a configuration change into the pick (`keycloak
realm_bootstrap`, `_master_login`, `provision_db`) applies it to something that is lost when the orphan is reaped, while
the converge reports success. One orphan source was removed (the oauth2-proxy kick no longer restarts Exited or Created
containers); anything else that leaves a stray container brings the coin flip back.

- **Behaviour:** one shared locate step asks swarm which task it wants, and every site above uses it. The fix belongs
  in `ansible/scripts/catena-container.sh`, which today takes the first line of a `docker ps` filtered by the swarm
  service-name label and `status=running`; the sites above do not call it yet. `docker service ps <stack>_<service>
  --filter desired-state=running --format '{{.Name}}.{{.ID}}'` names the live task; any other container carrying the
  name is an orphan by definition. A sweep for the same shape (`docker ps` then `head -n1`, or a label filter then
  `head -n1`) covers the rest of `ansible/` and `ansible/playbooks/filter_plugins/swarm_naming.py`.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test beside `ansible/tests/unit/` fails on any task file that pipes `docker ps` into `head -n1`;
  the listed sites pass it; a converge on a host with a stray Exited container of an app service still validates the
  live task (test-bench scenarios oauth2_proxy_cookie_rotation_round_trip, keycloak_master_realm_hardening,
  reconcile_is_a_noop).

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `ansible/scripts/catena-container.sh`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/swarm/defaults/main.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/infrastructure/defaults/main.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/swarm/tasks/main.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/swarm/tasks/validate.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/infrastructure/tasks/main.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/infrastructure/tasks/validate.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/tasks/_master_login.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/tasks/provision_db.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/tasks/realm_bootstrap.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/tasks/realm_export.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/tasks/validate.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/oauth2_proxy/tasks/validate.yml`
- EDIT: `ansible/reconcile/roles/postgres/tasks/main.yml`

### Implementation and verification
Install the shared helper in the swarm role before Postgres and Keycloak, removing its infrastructure installation. Support an explicit service name for standalone services. Intersect full desired task names (docker service ps --no-trunc) with locally running service-labelled containers; preserve query errors as errors. Each retry resolves anew. Run ShellCheck and affected Ansible unit tests with uv run python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider. Acceptance bench scenarios remain release verification; no live bench is available on this worker. Propose any SPEC row in the PR reserved-files section.

title: catena-restic-key.py writes the store back without the store lock
body:
`ansible/scripts/catena-restic-key.py` (:103-118, :355-356): generate and rotate load the store, run
`restic key passwd`, then write back the secrets and config sections they read (`_save_store`) with no store lock, so a
store write made meanwhile is lost.

- **Behaviour:** the script takes `/run/catena-store.lock` (fcntl `LOCK_EX`, as `onbox_config.store_lock`) around a
  re-read of the store and writes back only `backup_restic_password`.
- **Security notes:** none new; the store lock is the existing leaf lock.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test that a store write made during a rotation survives.

Part of catenahq/ops#117 (The backup password arms hold the whole server), which tracks the change across repositories.

title: The converge log carries per-task times
body:
`ansible/ansible.cfg`, `ansible/bootstrap/roles/ansible_runtime/defaults/main.yml` (`ansible_runtime_spec`),
`ansible/.gitignore`. No per-task time is recorded anywhere, so a slow converge (14 min for a domain apply) cannot be
broken down. The `ansible.posix.profile_tasks` callback does not resolve on a host: `ansible/.collections` is a
gitignored local install, and the host runtime is ansible-core alone (installed by install-host.sh and the
ansible_runtime role from "ansible-core>=2.20,<2.23"). Checked from the tree with its own ansible.cfg and the tree's
venv: `ansible-doc -t callback ansible.posix.profile_tasks` answers "was not found"; with
`ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH=ansible/.collections` it resolves (ansible.posix 2.2.2). Two options:

- Add ansible.posix to the host's Ansible runtime (an install step in the ansible_runtime role, a release-only
  infrastructure change), then set `callbacks_enabled = ansible.posix.profile_tasks` in `ansible/ansible.cfg`.
- A timing callback in the tree (GPL code copied into catena-ce).

Recommended: the collection, in a release. Coordinate with catenahq/catena-admin#249 and catenahq/ops#533 (the hash-locked Ansible environment), which change how the runtime is installed.

- **Behaviour:** every converge log carries the time of each task and a summary after the recap.
- **Security notes:** none beyond a pinned collection version in the runtime.
- **Acceptance:** a converge log holds per-task times.

Part of catenahq/ops#121 (The converge log carries per-task times), which tracks the change across repositories.

title: The recovery README restores only the newest snapshot
body:
`ansible/reconcile/roles/backup/templates/RECOVERY-README.en.md.j2` and `.fr.md.j2`, section 4, run
`restic restore latest`. A reader who restores an application the newest snapshot no longer holds (one removed since) is
not told how to choose an older snapshot.

- **Behaviour:** section 4 tells the reader to list the snapshots (`restic snapshots`), find one holding the
  application (`restic ls <id> <volume folder>`) and restore that one, in English and French.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** the rendered README's section 4 holds the three steps in both languages.

Part of catenahq/ops#144 (The recovery README restores only the newest snapshot), which tracks the change across repositories.

title: A domain change across Cloudflare accounts leaves the old tunnel
body:
The tunnel rotate on a domain change deletes the old tunnel by name in the new domain's account only, so when the old domain lives in another Cloudflare account that account keeps a connectorless tunnel and the old wildcard on it.

- **Behaviour:** after a move to a domain in another Cloudflare account, the old account holds no Catena tunnel and no Catena record.
- **Security notes:** uses the old zone's own token, kept until its zone is settled; no new secret.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test beside `ansible/tests/unit/test_tunnel_delete_outlasts_a_reconnect.py` with the old domain in another account.

The cross-repository tracking task covers the release-bench acceptance for this change.

### Files Scope

- `ansible/reconcile/roles/cloudflare_tunnel_regenerate/tasks/`: read outgoing zone tokens, resolve their accounts, reuse bounded tunnel deletion, and validate retired accounts. Preserve configured extra domains and retain tokens for the existing wildcard retirement handoff.
- `ansible/reconcile/roles/cloudflare_tunnel_regenerate/README.md`: document account-aware rotation.
- `ansible/tests/unit/test_tunnel_delete_outlasts_a_reconnect.py`, `ansible/tests/unit/test_cloudflare_tunnel_regenerate_validate.py`, and an adjacent cross-account regression test: exercise shipped tasks against a local Cloudflare stand-in.

### Verification

From `ansible`, run `uv run --locked python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` on the scoped test files and existing secret-bearing-task and role-validation checks. Use the locked ansible-core and Python >=3.13. Release bench: `primary_domain_change_round_trip` across two accounts and `cf_tunnel_regenerate_round_trip`. No live Cloudflare calls or bench VM are available to the worker.

### Implementation evidence

The store preserves outgoing tokens in `secrets.cloudflare_api_tokens`; `CLOUDFLARE_ZONES` entries after index zero are configured extra domains. catena-admin's existing `RetireZones` removes the old wildcard after the tunnel handoff and prunes settled tokens. Token lifecycle remains with that owner.

title: The marketplace token and the templates knob keep names for a catalog the panel no longer renders
body:
The token, its header (`X-Catena-Marketplace-Token`), its environment variable (`CATENA_MARKETPLACE_TOKEN`) and its store
key (`catena_marketplace_token`) guard only the panel's Keycloak forward. The templates knob `CATENAHQ_TEMPLATES_BASE`
was removed from catena-ce (6fb8a65); only the token's name is left to change.

- **Behaviour:** the token carries a name that says what it guards, renamed together in catena-ce (`ansible/helpers/onbox_config.py`, `ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/defaults/main.yml`, `ansible/SECRETS.md`) and in catena-admin (`shell/web/keycloakforward.go`, `payload/lib/http_util.py`).
- **Security notes:** the token is a panel secret; a rename touches the store key, the header and the bench specs
  together.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test that every name is read; the store key, the environment variable and the header carry the new name in catena-ce and catena-admin.

Part of catenahq/ops#339 (The marketplace token and the panel knobs keep names for a catalog the panel no longer renders), which tracks the change across repositories.

title: The version report is no longer a timer
body:
The panel reads the version report when a page opens, refreshing it when it is older than its age. The
`catena-version-check.timer` the infrastructure role enables goes, with a disable on servers that have it; the converge's
own run of the report stays. `catena-reboot-check.timer` stays for the alert.

- **Behaviour:** a converge enables no version-check timer and disables one left from before.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** the role's unit tests.

Part of catenahq/ops#379 (Panel cards computed when the page opens), which tracks the change across repositories.

title: The monitors' core wiring goes once the catalog has generic rules
body:
The monitors (Gatus, Healthchecks, Beszel) keep their wiring in core under fixed names, ports and keys: a gate, a

title: Supervisor health dashboard missing last_refresh marker (#118)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard body at #118 does not contain a `last_refresh: <ISO8601>` marker. Either the dashboard has never been rebuilt by the current version of `stats-health-dashboard.sh`, or the marker has been stripped from the body.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status.

   macOS / launchd:

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

   Linux / systemd user timers:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer --no-pager
   systemctl --user status aidevops-stats-wrapper.service --no-pager
   systemctl --user list-timers --all --no-pager 'aidevops*'
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/.config/systemd/user/aidevops-stats-wrapper.*
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/catenahq/catena-ce/issues/118 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **macOS missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **Linux missing or inactive systemd timer:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so the Linux scheduler setup reinstalls and enables `aidevops-stats-wrapper.timer` and `aidevops-stats-wrapper.service` under `~/.config/systemd/user`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 118 --repo catenahq/catena-ce` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: Managed-update manifest: gate proxies take patch updates
body:
The managed-update manifest (`ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/templates/managed-services.json.j2`) leaves oauth2-proxy out of the lane on purpose, so only the converge floor `OAUTH2_PROXY_IMAGE` moves the gate proxies' image. catena-admin#188 moves the gate proxies to patch releases through the lane; this item is the manifest line it needs.

- **Behaviour:** the manifest lists Catena's own oauth2-proxy instances with policy patch, a Quay upstream, and a ready check for the sign-in redirect. The per-host `oauth2-proxy-clients` services use the Swarm discovery implemented in catenahq/catena-admin#297, which deduplicates explicitly declared instances. The exclusion comment no longer names oauth2-proxy.
- **Security notes:** gate proxies guard every admin address; a patch that breaks sign-in is rolled back by the lane.
- **Acceptance:** the manifest renders with the new entries and its unit test passes; catena-admin#188 lands with it (merged through catenahq/catena-admin#297).

### Files Scope
- `ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/templates/managed-services.json.j2`
- `ansible/reconcile/roles/catena-admin/tasks/validate.yml`
- `ansible/tests/unit/test_managed_services_manifest.py`

Verification: from `ansible`, run `uv run python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_managed_services_manifest.py`. Match the ready command to the merged engine's sign-in redirect probe. Reserved SPEC text is proposed in the PR body.

title: The emailed sign-in code can be requested for any known client address
body:
Open, `ansible/reconcile/roles/keycloak/provider` (`CatenaClientEmailCodeAuthenticator.java`). Typing a client's
address on the sign-in page makes the server mail that client a code, up to 5 per sign-in (`MAX_SENDS`, one every 30 seconds) and as often as new sign-ins
are started; the page answers every address alike, so this reveals no account, but it can flood one mailbox and the
relay's quota. The mailing queue drops jobs past 100.

- **Behaviour:** codes to one address are limited per hour across sign-ins.
- **Security notes:** mail flooding of a client's mailbox, and the relay's sending quota.
- **Acceptance:** a provider test of the hourly limit; `catalog_app_sign_in` stage `stage-client-email-code` passes.

title: The ports card is only as fresh as the last install
body:
`installer/catena_installer/checks.py` `public_ports` scans the host's TCP ports from outside on every
`catena-installer install` and writes `/var/lib/catena/port-scan.json`, which the System tab's ports card and the
Business compliance panel read. A port an app opens later without a `vps.expose` label shows on neither until the
next install, and a bench host never gets a record (the installer skips a private address).

- **Behaviour:** the card and the compliance line reflect the host's exposure within a day, or say how old the scan
  is (the card shows its date).
- **Security notes:** an undeclared open port is the exposure this card exists to show.
- **Acceptance:** a decision on where an outside scan can run on a schedule (a host cannot scan its own public
  address from outside); then a unit test of the writer.

title: CODEOWNERS on the host hardening roles
body:
Malicious-PR review is human-only. Branch rulesets exist (`dev-updates`, `release-checks`, `release-main`, `release-tags`, `renovate-automerge-gate`) and there is no CODEOWNERS file in the repository.

- **Behaviour:** a CODEOWNERS file names an owner for the roles' hardening paths (`ansible/bootstrap/roles/common`), and a ruleset requires a code-owner review on them. The licence package is in catena-admin (`license/`); its CODEOWNERS entry is a separate catena-admin issue.
- **Security notes:** a pull request that weakens the host hardening needs a named human reviewer.
- **Acceptance:** `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers the hardening roles; the ruleset's code-owner requirement is on for them.
